answer: Yearly proof-of-life at the pension office stops Sybils: each identity appears before a wharf clerk who checks face and fingerprints against the onyx civil registry and stamps the timber pension roll. No stamp, no payout; one stand-in caught burns the whole batch because their forged papers share one source. One honest visit costs a morning; 1,000 fakes need 1,000 hired stand-ins, about $200 each, $200,000 a year, that die at the next check.
